name: Palo Alto Furniture Co.
note: First big tenant of the corner building at University & Bryant, which opened in 1900.

name: J.C. Penney
note: Penney's opened here in 1924 and was run for two decades by Merrill Vanderpool.

name: Walgreens (and Subway)
note: Walgreens from 1973; the 1900 building burned in an arson fire in July 2007 and was demolished.

name: Varsity Theatre (original)
note: Palo Alto's first Varsity, opened March 1912, showing stage shows and films.

name: Stanford Theatre
note: Opened June 9, 1925. Restored by the Packard family (1987-89); still shows classic films.

name: Varsity Theatre
note: Reid Brothers movie palace. Revival house and music venue in the 1970s.

name: Borders Books
note: Bookstore in the converted Varsity Theatre; closed when Borders liquidated in 2011.

name: HanaHaus & Blue Bottle Coffee
note: Co-working cafe in the old Varsity; closure announced Sept 2024.

name: Liddicoat's Market
note: Grocery and lunch market; building dates to 1923-24.

name: Z Gallerie
note: Home furnishings store in the old Liddicoat's building.

name: Apple Store (current)
note: Opened Oct 27, 2012 as a prototype glass-front store.

name: Swain's Music
note: Music store; locals say Jerry Garcia rented instruments here.

name: Apple Store (first)
note: Opened Oct 2001, one of Apple's first stores and Steve Jobs's local store.

name: Shoe Palace
note: Took over the original Apple Store space.

name: Chimaera Books & Music
note: Ground-floor bookstore in the 'lucky building' until 2000.

name: Google (first office)
note: Google's first real office, 1999, after Logitech. Later tenants: PayPal, Danger, Milo.

name: PayPal
note: Early PayPal offices upstairs in the 'lucky building'.

name: Facebook (first office)
note: Facebook's first Palo Alto office.

name: Facebook
note: Facebook's downtown HQ before moving to the Stanford Research Park.

name: Peninsula Creamery
note: Diner and soda fountain since 1923.

name: Bell's Books
note: New and used bookstore, family-run since 1935.

name: University Art
note: Art supply and framing store.

name: Palo Alto Sport Shop & Toy World
note: Sporting goods and toys from 1930.

name: Gotham Shop
note: First building of the Ramona Street architectural district (Pedro de Lemos, 1925).

name: Cardinal Hotel
note: Palo Alto's first non-frame hotel.

name: Hotel President
note: 1929 hotel, long used as apartments; reopened as a hotel (now Graduate by Hilton Palo Alto).

name: Shady Lane
note: Craft store, gallery and gift shop; moved to Menlo Park in 2015.

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: Early coffeehouse and folk venue; later moved.

name: Coupa Cafe
note: Venezuelan cafe, a startup meeting spot.

name: Il Fornaio
note: In the Garden Court Hotel.

name: Evvia Estiatorio
note: Greek restaurant.

name: Pizza A Go-Go
note: Pizza by the slice, open late on weekends. Business records give 1988 as its start; it later moved to 335 University Ave.

name: Copeland's Sports
note: Sporting goods store at University & Waverley, remembered open in the early 1990s. The Cheesecake Factory replaced it after a 2003 renovation.

name: The Cheesecake Factory
note: Opened in late 2003 in the former Copeland's building; closed May 26, 2018.

name: Roger's Deli
note: Deli on Ramona, around the corner from Peninsula Beauty Supply, remembered open in the early 1990s. Exact address and years unknown; pin placement approximate.

name: Stars Palo Alto
note: Jeremiah Tower's Palo Alto branch of San Francisco's Stars, in the former Gatehouse restaurant building. Became Spago in late 1997.

name: Spago Palo Alto
note: Wolfgang Puck's Spago took over the Stars space, opening Dec 15, 1997, and lasted about a dozen years.

name: Osteria Toscana
note: Tuscan restaurant on the ground floor of the Cardinal Hotel, at Hamilton & Ramona, since 1986.

name: Nobu Palo Alto
note: Nobu Matsuhisa's restaurant in the Epiphany Hotel.

name: Reach Fitness
note: Gym on High Street near Homer.

name: TAVERNA
note: Greek restaurant at Emerson & Homer, across from Whole Foods, open since April 2018.

name: Gordon Biersch Brewery Restaurant
note: Brewery-restaurant on Emerson; reinvented as Dan Gordon's in 2016.

name: Dan Gordon's
note: Dan Gordon's reboot of the Gordon Biersch space; Meyhouse is there now.

name: Aquarius Theatre
note: Twin-screen arthouse cinema; opened Oct 1, 1969 with Medium Cool and The Rain People. Run by Landmark Theatres since 1985; renovated in 2015 with larger screens and recliners.

name: Palo Alto Post Office
note: Birge Clark's Spanish Colonial post office.

name: Palo Alto Depot
note: Streamline Moderne train station (Southern Pacific, now Caltrain).

name: Sam's Chowder House
note: Downtown branch of the Half Moon Bay seafood restaurant. It opened in November 2013 in the former Campo 185 space and closed in December 2016, when the space was sold to Wahlburgers.

name: Marufuku Ramen
note: Hakata-style ramen chain, opened in 2026 in the former Starbucks space.

name: Palermo Ristorante
note: Small, family-owned Italian restaurant and a longtime University Avenue favorite, remembered open by 1991 (it may be older). It moved out in 2005; the space later became Chicken Ranch, Mint Leaf, Han Fine Korean Cuisine and Umami Burger.

name: Taxi's Hamburgers
note: Retro hamburger diner with booths, a counter and a jukebox at the corner of University and Waverley, part of a small Bay Area chain. Opened December 11, 1995; still open in 2008, closing year not yet confirmed.

name: Cafe Renaissance
note: Cozy Mediterranean-leaning cafe and restaurant across Hamilton from the Chase bank, known for dishes like gazpacho and house-made cheesecake. In the Palo Alto Weekly's dining listings from at least 2006 to 2008; Curry Up Now later took over the space. Exact years not yet confirmed.

name: Good Earth Restaurant and Bakery
note: Health-food restaurant and bakery from a national chain. It opened in March 1976 in the former House of Pies building and closed in 2001 when the owner retired.

name: Tallman's House of Foam
note: A longtime downtown foam shop that sold foam and made custom cases. Owner Bob Tallman took it over in the 1970s, and it quietly closed in early January 2020.

name: Mango Cafe
note: Caribbean restaurant serving Trinidad and Tobago cuisine, which moved here in early 1995 after about five years on University Avenue. Palo Alto Weekly reviewed it in 1995 and 1998; when it closed has not been confirmed.

name: Fran's Market
note: Longtime neighborhood market at Lytton and Gilman; the space became Mademoiselle Colette bakery in 2016–17. Opening year unknown; Fran's Smoke Shop was listed next door at 497 Lytton in the 1950s.

name: The Victorian on Lytton
note: Bed-and-breakfast inn in the 1896 Queen Anne-style Hannah Clapp House, which was converted to an inn in 1985–86. It closed around 2006 after water damage, and the house later held a women's resource center.

name: Lytton Roasting Company
note: Neighborhood coffee shop and roaster on the corner of Lytton, in business for many years before John's Cafe took over the space in 2012; some regulars remember it as the Palo Alto Roasting Company. Opening year not yet confirmed (open by 2007).

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: Revival of the 1959 University Avenue coffeehouse, opened in 1973 in the 1923 Cashel building at Emerson and Homer. The founding owner sold it in 1994.

name: St. Michael's Waiting Room
note: Small venue next door to St. Michael's Alley that held weekly poetry readings and open-mic nights, in the spirit of the original 1959 coffeehouse. It closed around the time the restaurant was sold in 1994; its opening year is uncertain.

name: La Morenita
note: Family-run Mexican restaurant at Emerson and Homer that opened in May 1994 and closed in December 2017 when the owners retired. The Greek restaurant Taverna later took over the space.

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: California bistro run by the owners who bought St. Michael's Alley in 1994, in the space next door to the 800 Emerson original. The restaurant later moved to Homer Avenue, and the Emerson space served as its Annex until Taverna took it over around 2019.

name: Mandarin Gourmet
note: Chinese restaurant that was at this address for many years, until about 2014. Bird Dog opened in the space in late 2015.

name: Blue Chalk Cafe
note: Southern restaurant and bar across from City Hall, with blue felt pool tables and shuffleboard. It opened around 1992 and closed in early 2010.

name: University AME Zion Church
note: Palo Alto's oldest Black church, founded in 1918, worshipped in this building from its dedication in 1925 until moving to Middlefield Road around 1965. The preserved building later became part of a commercial development.

name: Vivre
note: Fitness and wellness studio on Emerson Street that offered yoga, cardio, Pilates, childcare and massage. It opened in May 2003 and closed around 2018; the street number is reported but not confirmed.

name: Barker Hotel
note: Residential hotel built in 1928 that came to house very low-income residents. The Palo Alto Housing Corporation (now Alta Housing) acquired it in 1994, and it still operates as affordable single-room-occupancy housing.

name: The Camera Shop
note: Downtown camera store that advertised in the 1961 Palo Alto High School yearbook. It is remembered as closing in the mid-1970s, and some of its staff later worked at Keeble & Shuchat; actual years open may be longer.

name: Lucky Store
note: Lucky supermarket, listed at this address in directories from 1950 through 1965; actual years open may be longer.

name: Palo Alto Police Department
note: Palo Alto's first combined police and fire station, a 1927 Birge Clark building. The police moved to the new City Hall around 1970, and the building later became the Avenidas senior center.

name: Uforia Studios
note: Boutique fitness studio with dance-based, cycling and strength classes, housed in the restored former University AME Zion Church building. It was listed at this address by 2011 and featured in a 2013 Palo Alto Weekly story on downtown boutique gyms.

name: FORM Fitness
note: Downtown gym founded in 2003 on Forest Ave; won the city lease for the new building at 445 Bryant St in 2004 and moved there in 2005, operating for nearly two decades until it was evicted in 2022 after falling behind on rent.

name: Zibibbo
note: Pan-Mediterranean restaurant in a renovated yellow Victorian house spanning Kipling to Waverley; opened in 1997 and closed in April 2014 after a 17-year run, after which the space became offices.

name: Vino Locale
note: Wine bar and kitchen in a century-old house, opened in January 2005 by Randy Robinson and a partner. Still operating, with live music in its back garden.

name: Palo Alto Fire Station 1
note: Downtown Palo Alto's main fire station, still in service, housing a fire engine and a paramedic ambulance. The year it opened is not confirmed.

name: Q Cafe & Billiards
note: Restaurant, nightclub and pool hall in a warehouse-style building on Alma Street, with billiards, live music and DJ nights. It opened in 1994 on a 10-year lease and was set to close at the end of July 2004, when the lease ran out.

name: Dragon Theatre
note: Small black-box theater with about 40 seats at the corner of Alma and Hamilton, run by Dragon Productions Theatre Company. It opened in February 2006 with The Heidi Chronicles and moved to a larger space in Redwood City in 2012.

name: Antique Interiors West
note: Antique furnishings shop in the former Thompson's Bakery building, mentioned in the Palo Alto Weekly in 1998; actual years open may be longer.

name: Museum of American Heritage
note: A museum of American technology and everyday life, housed in the restored 1907 Williams House and garden. It opened to the public there in April 1998 and is still open.

name: Woman's Club of Palo Alto
note: Clubhouse of the Woman's Club of Palo Alto, a civic and philanthropic group founded in 1894. The Tudor-Craftsman building by Charles Edward Hodges opened in 1916 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

name: California Yoga Center
note: Yoga studio with classes from beginner to advanced, listed at this address in local guides from 2006 and 2011. The studio later moved to Mountain View, and its years at this address may have been longer.

name: St. Michael's Alley
note: Long-running Palo Alto restaurant founded as a coffeehouse in 1959. After years at 806 Emerson St, the owners expanded into this larger dining space on Homer Ave in 2009; the 2011 Palo Alto Weekly Best Of lists the Homer Ave address for lunch and dinner, and the restaurant still operates there.

name: House of Bagels
note: A bagel shop on University Avenue that appeared in Palo Alto Weekly's Best Of winners lists. In late January 2015, after 27 years in business, its owner moved it to Edgewood Plaza on Embarcadero Road.

name: Robaii Falafel
note: Family-run Persian restaurant at Hamilton Ave and Cowper St, in the former Penny Farthing space. Opened in May 1998 serving falafel, hummus, baba ghanoush and lamb pitas, and closed in April 2010 after 12 years; Siam Orchid later took the space.

name: Maddalena's
note: Elegant white-tablecloth Continental restaurant at 544 Emerson St. Fred Maddalena took over the former Golden Dragon space in 1976 and ran it for 31 years; it served its last meal on May 19, 2007 after the landlord did not renew the lease.

name: United Nations Association Gift Shop
note: Volunteer-run gift shop selling UNICEF cards and fair-trade crafts from around the world, known locally as the UNICEF store. Created in 1974, it moved to its Emerson Street storefront just north of Hamilton Ave and is still operating there.

name: Miyake
note: Noisy, flashy sushi restaurant in the historic Fraternal Hall building, famous for sake bombs and a loud, crowded bar scene. It ran for about 25 years before closing in September 2012.

name: Lavanda Restaurant and Wine Bar
note: Mediterranean Italian restaurant and wine bar with a 600-bottle list that took over the former Good Earth space at the corner of University and Emerson in 2002. It closed in summer 2012 and was replaced by Campo 185.

name: Caffe Verona
note: Beloved downtown coffeehouse and Italian cafe that moved to 236 Hamilton Ave in 1984 and closed August 31, 2003 after 19 years, when its landlord declined to renew the lease. It was a famous meeting spot for entrepreneurs and neighborhood regulars.

name: Patxi's Chicago Pizza
note: Chicago-style deep-dish pizzeria that opened in 2004 as the first restaurant of the Patxi's chain. Listings now show this location as closed, reportedly around 2022.

name: Ramona's Pizza
note: Long-running downtown pizzeria and Stanford-student gathering spot; the owner bought it in 1978 and it closed in 2003, after which the Old Pro took over the space.

name: BayLeaf Cafe
note: Vegan cafe that took over the former Double Rainbow ice cream parlor space; reviewed in February 2003 and closed in October 2006.

name: L'Amie Donia
note: French bistro run by chef-owner Donia Bijan, opened in 1994 and rated Palo Alto's top restaurant by Zagat in 2004. It closed in early June 2004, and the new owner planned to reopen it as a French bistro called La Cheminee.

name: Darshana Yoga
note: Yoga studio founded by Catherine De Los Santos. It opened on this block of High Street in July 2003 and ran until 2012, and it was featured in the Palo Alto Weekly's Best of 2006 yoga category.

name: Reach Fitness Club
note: Downtown gym that opened in Palo Alto in 1982 and ran its fitness center at 707 High St. (listed there in the 1994 Best of) for 36 years, closing Dec. 15, 2018; its Pilates studio at 833 Emerson St. stayed open.

name: Palo Alto Bimmer
note: Independent BMW and MINI auto repair shop that opened in January 1980 at the 1929 gas station premises on Alma Street and still operates there; reviews and city permits place it at 799 Alma St. through the 2000s.

name: Kanpai Sushi
note: Family-owned Japanese restaurant serving sushi at 330 Lytton Ave since at least 2007, when it was named Palo Alto's best sushi spot; still operating there.

name: Spot A Pizza Place
note: Pizza restaurant that moved downtown around late 2008 after five years at Town & Country Village, taking over the former Espresso Bettola coffee house space. It closed abruptly in November 2017.

name: California Pizza Kitchen
note: Downtown branch of the California Pizza Kitchen chain, described in a 2005 review as 11 years old. It closed in mid-August 2014, while the chain's Stanford Shopping Center location stayed open.

name: Avenidas
note: Senior services center in the city-owned 1927 Birge Clark former police and fire station, opened around 1977–78 by the Senior Coordinating Council, which later took the name Avenidas. The building was renovated and expanded, reopening in 2019.

name: Downtown Library
note: The Downtown Branch of the Palo Alto Public Library opened here on March 8, 1971, across from the new Civic Center. It replaced the Carnegie library, which was demolished in 1967. The branch was renovated in 2011 and is still open.

name: Chimera Books and Music
note: Used bookstore in an 1897 house, listed at this address in 1982. Around 1990 it moved to University Avenue, and in 1999 it left for Redwood City.

name: Commuter Shell Service
note: Full-service Shell gas station on the corner of Alma St and Lytton Ave, run by the same operators for 42 years; downtown Palo Alto's only gas station, open around the clock, until Shell pulled out and it closed at the end of June 2010. The site later became the Lytton Gateway building.

name: YogaSource
note: Heated Bikram yoga studio that opened in May 1995, said to be the first outside San Francisco to offer heated yoga. It moved to Hamilton Avenue in 2001.

name: Ellison's Body Shop
note: Family-run auto body repair and towing shop founded May 1, 1929 by Earl Ellison Sr.; by 1995 it was one of only two body shops left downtown, and it ceased business in 2000. The building remains as a historical site.

name: Palo Alto Medical Clinic
note: Group medical practice in the Spanish Colonial Revival Roth Building, designed by Birge Clark in 1932. The clinic later moved out, and the city bought the building in 2000 to become the home of the Palo Alto History Museum.

name: The Photographer's Gallery
note: Fine art photography gallery at 732 Emerson St for 13 years; owner Amy Saret moved it to 536 Ramona St on Aug. 1, 1995, and the women's clothing store Virtuelle took over the Emerson space that October.

name: Smith Andersen Gallery
note: Fine art gallery run by Paula Kirkeby, opened in October 1969 at 200 Homer St and later at 728 Emerson St. It closed Aug. 1, 1996.

name: Florentine Restaurant and Pasta Market
note: Northern Italian restaurant and fresh pasta market, part of a San Jose-based chain owned by the Del Monaco family. Palo Alto Weekly readers voted it Best Pasta in 1994 and 1996; the years shown are the earliest and latest sources found, and it likely operated longer.

name: The Adventures of Jerusha
note: Women's clothing store at 515 Cowper St selling colorful easy-care separates in natural fibers and custom-made outfits; featured in Palo Alto Weekly Shop Talk in June and December 1995. Years shown are the first and last years sources confirm it at this address.

name: The Artifactory
note: Craft shop and studio that held art workshops such as mask-making, listed in the Palo Alto Weekly in 1994. A craft shop on this block was forced out when a fire destroyed the one-story building at Hamilton and Emerson around 1996.

name: La Pastaia Ristorante Italiano
note: Italian restaurant known for its duck-and-ricotta spinach ravioli. The Palo Alto Weekly reviewed it in 1993 and still listed it in 1994, and Evvia later took over the space.

name: Max's Eatz
note: Upscale deli offshoot of Max's Opera Cafe serving New York deli-style sandwiches, reviewed as new in April 1995. It closed within months, and World Wrapps was planned for the corner space by October 1995.

name: World Wrapps
note: Wrap and smoothie restaurant, a branch of a San Francisco chain, that was planned for the former Max's Eatz corner space in October 1995. It was listed here in a 1996 local food guide, but its exact opening and closing years are unknown.

name: Noah's Bagels
note: New York-style bagel shop at the corner of University and Bryant, voted Palo Alto's best bagels in 1995 and for years after; the building that housed Noah's and Starbucks was slated for demolition in August 2008.

name: Cafe Fino
note: Fred Maddalena's smaller art-deco nightclub next door to Maddalena's restaurant, sharing its kitchen and menu with live jazz, cabaret acts and tango lessons; it opened in 1989 and closed shortly after Maddalena's shut in May 2007.
